line: Crowley's Atu 0 in his own sentences: its number, letter and element, and the path that joins the Crown to Wisdom.

sections.title: What Crowley says the card is
sections.line: The number zero, the letter Aleph, and the element Air.

quotes.quote: The really important feature of this card is that its number should be 0. It represents therefore the Negative above the Tree of Life, the source of all things.
This card is attributed to the letter Aleph, which means an Ox, but by its shape the Hebrew letter (so it is said) represents a plough‐ share; thus the significance is primarily Phallic.
It is the equation of the Universe, the initial and final balance of the opposites; Air, in this card, therefore quintessentially means a vacuum.

sections.title: Its path on the Tree
sections.line: The chapter names only Kether; the appendix names Wisdom and the Crown as the two ends. The Key Scale gives path 11, and Crowley identifies Wisdom with Chokmah in the Emperor chapter.

quotes.quote: Kether: see the position of the Path of Aleph on the Tree of Life.
though Wisdom be the Second Emanation of His Essence, there is a path to separate and to join them,
the Reference thereof being Aleph, that is One indeed,
the Summit of Wisdom is the Opening of the Way that leadeth unto the Crown and Essence of all
This is the Path of the Pure Fool.
His authority is derived from Chokmah, the creative Wisdom, the Word, and is exerted upon Tiphareth, the organized man.

sections.title: What the card figures
sections.line: Crowley's own description of the Fool as the negative, and of the Universe as its manifestation.

quotes.quote: The Fool is of the gold of air.
The Fool is the negative issuing into manifestation; the Universe is that manifestation, its purpose accomplished, ready to return.
